newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North says year result to show improvement.
newsitem.headline: North says year result to show improvement.

text.p: Forestry and mining group North Ltd said on Monday its full year result for 1996/97 (July-June) was expected to show some improvement over 1995/96.

"The improved financial performance in the quarter is expected to continue for the remainder of the financial year and, despite the absence of abnormal tax benefits which were recorded in the fourth quarter of last year, the full year result is now expected to show some improvement over 1996," managing director Campbell Anderson said in a statement accompanying the third quarter result.
North said net profit in the three months ended March 31 rose to A$39.2 million from A$19.0 million a year earlier and nine month profits rose to A$89.2 million from A$51.3 million.
The company achieved net earnings of A$111.89 million in 1995/96 (July-June) from A$116.37 million a year ago.

Anderson said North continued to make progress towards meeting performance improvements from 1997/98 and beyond with the introduction of new projects such as the Alumbrera copper and gold project in Argentina and the purchase of a controlling stake in Iron Ore Co of Canada earlier in calendar 1997.

He also said the company expected to increase uranium production from mid-1997 and would progressively increase wood fibre exports. North owns 68 percent of uranium miner Energy Resources of Australia Ltd.

"In moving towards the Year 2000, North has committed to a feasibility study on the West Angelas iron ore project in the Pilbara, and continues the approval processes for the Jabiluka uranium mine in the Northern Territory and the Lake Cowal gold mine in New South Wales," Anderson said.
North, a mining house based in Melbourne, has a 25 percent stake in the Alumbrera project, the same stake as that held by Canada's Rio Algom Ltd.
MIM Ltd has a 50 percent stake and last week dismissed rumours that it planned to merge with North.
